definition: A quantity that has magnitude only, with no direction, such as mass, distance, speed, energy or temperature.
A quantity that has both magnitude and direction, such as displacement, velocity, acceleration or force; it is drawn as an arrow whose length shows its size.
Combining vectors by drawing them head to tail, so the resultant runs from the tail of the first to the head of the last; to subtract a vector, add its negative.
Replacing a vector by two perpendicular components that add up to it; at angle $\theta$ to the $x$-direction they are $F\cos\theta$ and $F\sin\theta$.
The angle at the centre of a circle when the arc it cuts off equals the radius, so $\theta = \frac{s}{r}$ and $2\pi$ rad $= 360^{\circ}$.
